prompt.intro: Tell me the residential electricity rate for {0}. {1}
prompt.onlyJson: Reply with only the JSON below, no explanation.
prompt.rule.currency: 1. Currency is the ISO 4217 code; Symbol is the symbol actually used there.
prompt.rule.billingDay: 2. BillingCycleStartDay is the day the billing period restarts (usually 1).
prompt.rule.fixedCharge: 3. FixedChargePerMonth is any monthly standing charge that does not depend on usage. Use 0 if there is none.
prompt.rule.taxes: 4. Taxes use a fraction, so 10% is 0.1. If tax is already included in the per-kWh price, leave the array empty and say so in one line outside the JSON.
prompt.rule.rate: 5. Rate takes whichever of these three shapes matches the local tariff:
prompt.rate.tiered: Tiered, where the price rises with usage:
prompt.rate.tieredNote: The last tier's UpToKwh must be null.
prompt.rate.tou: Time of use, where the price depends on the hour:
prompt.rate.touNote: Days is all / mon-fri / sat,sun; times are 24-hour HH:MM.
prompt.rule.budget: 6. Leave MonthlyBudget at 0. I will set that myself.
prompt.rule.uncertain: 7. If you are unsure, use the most common residential tariff and note in one line outside the JSON which year the rates are from.

tray.pawnio.title: JuiceBar — precise measurement
tray.pawnio.body:
Reading CPU power needs the PawnIO driver.

PawnIO is a signed, open-source kernel driver that hardware monitoring tools use to reach model-specific registers.

JuiceBar runs without it: GPU power is still measured properly, and the CPU share is estimated from utilisation instead.

Open the download page?
tray.elevate.title: Measure the CPU directly?
tray.elevate.body:
The PawnIO driver is installed, but reading CPU power through it needs administrator rights. JuiceBar can restart with those rights now.

Skip it and JuiceBar keeps working — GPU power is still measured and the CPU share is estimated, which the badge in the popup says plainly.
wizard.title: JuiceBar — Electricity rate
wizard.heading: Electricity rate
wizard.intro: Rates differ everywhere and are structured differently too. Rather than filling in a form, ask an assistant: copy the prompt below, paste it in, and paste the reply straight back.
wizard.step1: Enter where you live and copy the prompt
wizard.regionHint: e.g. Seoul / KRW · Berlin / EUR — currency is optional
wizard.copyFailed: Could not reach the clipboard. Select the text below and copy it by hand.
wizard.step2Hint: Explanation around it is fine — only the JSON is read.
wizard.exportCurrentTip: Puts the active rate here as JSON so you can edit it directly
wizard.exportedHint: These are your current settings. Edits are read as you type.
wizard.budgetHint: The gauge treats this as a full tank. Leave it empty to gauge against power instead.
wizard.needsRate: Paste the assistant's reply above. Without a rate there is nothing to cost.
wizard.budgetNotNumber: The budget is not a number.
settings.title: JuiceBar — Settings
settings.tariffNotSet: Not set yet. Costs cannot be worked out without a rate.
settings.budgetHint: The gauge treats this as a full tank. Leave it empty to gauge against power instead.
settings.resetHint: Clears what has piled up since the cycle started. Useful after changing your rate, or when trial runs inflated the total. Earlier cycles are left alone.
settings.resetConfirm: Reset this cycle's total to zero? This cannot be undone.
settings.gauge.budget: Cost — how much of the budget this cycle has used
settings.gauge.instant: Power — how many watts right now
settings.autoStart: Start when I sign in to Windows
settings.autoStartHint: Starts quietly at logon. If JuiceBar is running as administrator it registers a scheduled task instead, so no UAC prompt appears.
settings.version: Version {0} · checks GitHub Releases once a day.
settings.versionDev: Version {0} · development builds do not replace themselves.
settings.channelsHint: Which power sensors go into the total. Sensor names and meanings differ by hardware, so the automatic choice can be wrong. If the total is higher than reality, something is being counted twice.
settings.sensor.noPawnIo: No energy meter on this machine, so the CPU share is estimated. The PawnIO driver plus administrator rights would measure it instead.
settings.sensor.elevated: PawnIO installed and running as administrator — CPU power is measured, so the values below are unused.
settings.sensor.notElevated: PawnIO is installed but JuiceBar is not running as administrator, so the CPU share is estimated.
settings.sensor.energyMeter: The Windows energy meter is measuring CPU power directly — no driver needed.
settings.diagnosticsHint: Whether power can be measured depends on your exact machine. This copies what JuiceBar sees — Windows version, sensors, and what it is summing — as a block you can paste into a bug report. It carries no machine name, no file paths and no usage or prices.
settings.error.budget: The budget is not a number.

settings.error.noChannel: At least one power channel has to stay selected.

settings.error.autoStartAdmin: Turning autostart off needs administrator rights, because it was registered as a scheduled task.
calib.title: JuiceBar — Calibration
calib.heading: Calibrate with a wattmeter
calib.intro: Nothing can measure your motherboard, drives and fans, or the losses in the power supply, so those are estimated. Tell JuiceBar what a plug-in wattmeter or an energy-monitoring smart plug reads and it will work out the real figures for this machine.
calib.hint: Two readings are needed, far enough apart: one while the machine is idle, and one under load from a game or a render.
calib.inputHint: Enter what the wattmeter shows, in watts.
calib.needSecond: (one more reading needed — take it under load)
calib.notNumber: Please enter a number, for example 385
calib.outOfRange: The value has to be between 0 and 5000 W.
calib.notReady: No sensor reading yet. Please try again in a moment.
calib.done: Calibrated — {0} W for the parts nothing can measure, power supply efficiency {1}. Wall power is now worked out from these.
